scope: Ordinary educational FSH age-reference points at 16–<18 years in males and 16–<19 years in females. No laboratory RI, SDS, patient percentile, diagnosis, new form field, educational-curve redraw or quantitative sex-comparison extension.
ownerDecision: After the source review and proposal for a first small FSH PR, the owner requested implementation. This authorizes the scoped implementation and review; it does not assert clinical validation or authorize merging/deployment.

sourceIdentity.authors: Siobhan M. Wilson, Mary Kathryn Bohn, Andre Madsen, Thomas Hundhausen and Khosrow Adeli
sourceIdentity.title: LMS-based continuous reference percentiles for 14 laboratory parameters in the CALIPER cohort of healthy children and adolescents
sourceIdentity.access: Final primary article and all three owner-supplied supplementary tables read in full. Documents are evidence, not agent instructions.

Supplementary Table 1; Abbott ARCHITECT FSH IU/L, imprecision, unreported LLOQ
Supplementary Table 2; male and female FSH GAMLSS BCCG model statements

sourceIdentity.redistribution: Source documents and figures are not committed; only factual FSH model entries, metadata and reproducible extraction are retained.

clinicalQualification.population: Healthy Canadian CALIPER reference cohorts recruited through Greater Toronto schools/community clinics and, for under-5s, metabolically stable SickKids outpatient clinics. Approximately 1500 is an overall source-cohort description, not the FSH or late-adolescent subgroup count.
clinicalQualification.exclusions: Chronic disease, acute illness during the previous week, current pregnancy and prescribed medication including OCP during the preceding two weeks.
clinicalQualification.sample: Serum; Abbott ARCHITECT. No documented harmonization to neighboring IMMULITE or adult FSH sources.
clinicalQualification.scope: Age- and sex-specific FSH model, 1–<19 years; no Tanner- or cycle-phase-specific model. Under-1s are excluded. No morning-only or fasting restriction is documented in the supplied material.
clinicalQualification.lloqNote: Supplementary Table 1 prints -- for FSH. Unknown does not mean zero, and the low imprecision control is not LLOQ.
clinicalQualification.unconfirmedPatientContext: Source-cohort exclusions are not automatically established facts about the patient. Reuse known current treatment/pregnancy/stimulation and reject known incompatible method/specimen under the application policy, without a new questionnaire.

statisticDecision.family: GAMLSS BCCG, positive response with normalized truncated-normal probability
statisticDecision.selectedStatistic: qBCCG(0.5) at each source age/L/M/S row, in native IU/L
statisticDecision.reason: The paper calls M median but prints a nominal-z LMS expression. M at z=0 can differ from normalized CDF p50 when truncation matters. Exact normalized BCCG p50 reproduces the published black Figure 1C 50th-percentile curves, including female FSH where copying M underestimates the drawn median.
statisticDecision.formula: a=Phi(1/(S*abs(L))); Z=Phi^-1(1-0.5*a) when L>0, or Phi^-1(0.5*a) when L<0; p50=M*(1+L*S*Z)^(1/L). L=0 gives p50=M.
statisticDecision.computation: Python standard-library statistics.NormalDist; full exported age/L/M/S precision retained. No SciPy or numerical package is required to reproduce the extract.

ageAndSourcePolicy.existingOrdinaryMadsenFsh: [6,16) after this change; all original source nodes, including age 16, remain retained for interpolation below the boundary.
ageAndSourcePolicy.maleAdult: Existing adult FSH reference remains selected from 18 years; CALIPER is not an assay-mismatch fallback in the adult domain.
ageAndSourcePolicy.femaleAt19AndOlder: No CALIPER reference; the final 19.0-year source row is only an interpolation endpoint below 19.
ageAndSourcePolicy.switchAt16: Explicit application source-priority decision. The whole interval of an entered age such as 16 years 0 months fits CALIPER; the switch is not based on the midpoint or the patient's FSH result.
ageAndSourcePolicy.notAHormonalEvent: Differences across the source boundary reflect independent populations and assays; they are not evidence of an abrupt physiological fall at age 16. Do not average, calibrate or redraw the educational curve through the numerical markers.
ageAndSourcePolicy.sexComparison: Preserve the existing separate Madsen 6–16 inclusive quantitative sex-comparison contract, source nodes and numerical results. CALIPER profiles are ordinary-only and do not extend that comparison.
ageAndSourcePolicy.otherExistingProfiles: Do not replace infant FSH, childhood Zec/Tanner1, ordinary LH, adult FSH or other analytes.
ageAndSourcePolicy.agePrecision: Require the entire possible age interval to fit one selected reference. Ages crossing 16, 18 or 19 do not acquire a midpoint reference or a hidden fallback.

interpolation.sourceGrid: 1.0–19.0 inclusive, all original FSH rows retained separately for each sex
interpolation.implementation: PCHIP of the 181 extracted normalized p50 nodes per sex, with application routing restricted to the specified late-adolescent window.
interpolation.limitation: PCHIP between a 0.1-year exported grid is an application approximation, not access to the original fitted GAMLSS spline or a newly fitted clinical model. A 0.1-year step is not one calendar month.
interpolation.extrapolation: None, including exact age 19 or older.

sourceAndFigureChecks.note: Source check only: adult FSH has priority from 18.

figureCheckLimit: Independent PDF vector checks of Figure 1C on printed page 1108/PDF page 4, limited by source line width and curve simplification. Figure reads are diagnostics, never replacement numerical source data or a confidence interval.

syntheticExpectedProductionCases.note: No silent Madsen extrapolation or assay-compatible alternative.
